subject: Monthly token runway + procurement gating — post-demo follow-up

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: Monthly token runway + procurement gating — post-demo follow-up

Thanks again for a great demo earlier, Alex — appreciate the open discussion about integration patterns and expected load. Quick recap + the numbers we sketched on the call so your procurement team can start sizing approvals. Attach: avery-demo-deck.pdf, runway-sensitivity-forecast.xlsx (attached).

1) User / request assumptions we used (two scenarios)
- Conservative: 25k MAU, 1 request per user/day, avg 800 tokens/request -> ~600M tokens/month across the product (note: this is total tokens; we bucket generation/embedding mixes in the attached sheet).
- Pilot/Aggressive: 150k MAU, 2 requests per user/day, avg 800 tokens/request -> ~24B tokens/month (we recommended a staged rollout; attached sensitivity matrix shows burn at incremental rollouts).

2) Unit economics (example pricing bands)
- Pay-as-you-go: $60 / 1M tokens (no commit)
- 12-month committed: $40 / 1M tokens (recommended if monthly spend > $10k)
- Target we used for internal ROI modeling: $45 / 1M tokens (midpoint)

3) Preliminary monthly spend band (based on scenarios above & unit prices)
- Conservative (50M–300M tokens range in pilot phases): ~$2.5k — $15k / month (at $50 / 1M).
- Larger scale (1B+ tokens): plan on $40–$60k / month depending on commit/quantization and caching gains.

4) Procurement thresholds you mentioned on the call (please confirm):
- PO required for vendors with recurring spend > $10k / month (or > $120k / year).
- Legal prefers a simple SOW + a one-page commercial summary for initial PO.

As next steps: can you confirm the procurement contact and whether the PO threshold you quoted is formal? I can produce an itemized 6-month forecast and a short SOW for review (I attached a draft forecast to speed approvals). Monica, can you review the attached sensitivity sheet and flag any technical caveats we should call out for procurement? Karthik, can you add a short note on Dedicated/reserved capacity pricing delta if they want predictability once they cross the $120k/yr boundary?

Thanks — happy to sync live with procurement if it helps accelerate.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0193

Thanks, Priyom — helpful recap and concrete numbers. A few notes from procurement/finance side: 

- Preliminary internal budget: we are comfortable allocating ~$5k–$12k / month to start for a 3–6 month pilot. That aligns with your conservative pilot band.
- Procurement rule (confirmed): PO required for recurring spend > $10k / month OR suppliers with > $120k annual exposure. If your commercial summary can show a 6-month forecast under $120k, we can sign PO with standard terms.
- Procurement contact is Maria Lopez (cc'd). She prefers an itemized cost forecast (monthly token volumes x $/1M) + a short SOW that states scope and trial objectives.

Requests: please send the itemized 6-month forecast and a one-page commercial summary (line items + recommended PO trigger). If you have a short SOW template, attach it; Maria will circulate to legal.

Also, curious on what kind of unit-econ improvements we should expect if we adopt prefix caching + a lightweight reranking step (we discussed caching gains briefly). If you can quantify that in the forecast, even as an optimistic vs conservative delta, that will help approvals.

Happy to jump on a procurement call next week if needed.

—Alex
Alex Cho | CTO, Avery Solutions
alex.cho@averysolutions.com

Subject: Re: Monthly token runway + procurement gating — post-demo follow-up

Alex — thanks, and great to have Maria looped in. Quick answers / attachments: I updated the attached runway-sensitivity-forecast.xlsx to include an itemized 6-month forecast and a small appendix showing caching + KV-prefix savings (conservative: 10% token reduction; optimistic: 30% with aggressive prefix reuse + client-side caching). See the "optimizations" tab.

Commercial options we propose (summary):
- Option A (Pay-as-you-go): $60 / 1M tokens, no commit, immediate onboarding. Good for small pilots and exploratory traffic.
- Option B (12-month commit): $40 / 1M tokens + 10% additional credits for first month, requires monthly billing with PO or card on file. Recommended if expected month-to-month spend > $10k.
- Option C (Dedicated reserved capacity): custom pricing, typically 15–30% discount vs committed rate for heavy steady-state (requires capacity sizing; Karthik will provide estimated delta).

Procurement language for your team to circulate: we can provide a one-page commercial summary that includes the chosen option, expected monthly forecast line items (tokens x $/1M), billing cadence, and standard Redwood T&Cs. If the PO rule is > $10k/mo OR > $120k/yr then Option B will likely be the route to secure better unit economics.

Attachments: runway-sensitivity-forecast.xlsx (updated) and a one-page commercial summary draft (I included it as the first tab in the workbook).

Next steps: 
- Monica: can you validate the optimization assumptions (10% / 30%) and add any technical caveats for the SOW?
- Karthik: please add a short note on Dedicated sizing + expected cost delta for a 12–18 month commit (I put a placeholder cell in the workbook).
- Alex / Maria: if you can confirm the formal PO threshold and whether your procurement team needs any onboarding docs, I will prepare the SOW and send everything in a single packet for review.

Thanks — I can also do a 20-min procurement walk-through next Tue/ Wed.

Best,
Priyom
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
